leading_positions.synthesis: Five of eleven members name B005 as their preferred prize part, one short of the six needed. All five name the same laureates: Pakes, Berry and Levinsohn. Friberg's opening had Bresnahan as third name and he revised it to Levinsohn in round 1. Enflo moved to B005 from B025 after reading the openings. Shared reasoning: Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes demand estimation is the cleanest attribution core, the methods are about three decades old, and they are widely used in merger review, antitrust, regulation, trade, health and environmental work. Citation wording is not identical. Teorell explicitly adds dynamic industry models, and others frame it around demand and competition, market power or merger analysis. Every supporter also names the same main reservations: it is a methods or toolkit contribution without a single headline finding, BLP estimates are sensitive to implementation, and the three-name cap excludes Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin. Supporters differ somewhat on how much weight those reservations carry.

Two members (including the chair, who discloses this) prefer B014 with Persson, Tabellini and Besley. Both describe a mature, unified theory-to-evidence programme on how electoral rules, constitutions and state capacity shape fiscal policy and development, and both treat the three-person set as coherent. Both concede the same two weaknesses: cross-country identification is weaker than design-based work, and the 2024 institutions prize may make the contribution look less distinct. Both argue it is distinct (policy choice under given rules versus long-run historical origins of institutions). Fredriksson names a Persson-Tabellini two-person core as a fallback and says Besley's state-capacity strand is the part most exposed to the overlap objection. Hassler states he would move to B005 if the overlap were judged decisive. Fredriksson lists B005 as his main alternative.

Two members prefer B027 with Kiyotaki and Moore only. They agree that the collateral-constraint amplification mechanism is a conceptual advance with a clean two-person attribution, that it is thoroughly absorbed into macro-financial modelling, and that Gertler and Gilchrist (the accelerator strand tied to Bernanke) should not be added. Both state the same weaknesses: empirical validation is indirect, and the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises is adjacent. Both name B005 as an alternative and acknowledge its documented record of use. They differ on the comparison criterion. Krusell weights conceptual originality over number of fields using a tool. Boppart would apply breadth of use equally to Kiyotaki-Moore and was moved by the B005 argument.

Two members prefer B030 with Autor, Hanson and Dorn. Both rest the case on design-based evidence and a framework that explains it, with the China-shock design treated as a joint Autor-Dorn-Hanson contribution. Both exclude Katz, citing overlap of his skill-bias strand with the 2023 prize, and both would keep the citation anchored in the empirical labour-demand effects of technology and trade shocks rather than claim the whole task framework. Dreber moved here from B009 (her opening first choice) on replication depth and maturity. Both acknowledge that the persistence and magnitude of the trade-shock effects and shift-share identification remain debated. Neither claims settled maturity. Both list B005 as an alternative.

areas_of_agreement: Each of the eleven members prefers a single prize part, and the explicit first-choice split is B005 five, B014 two, B027 two and B030 two. No ballot has six explicit supporters.

Within each leading ballot, all explicit supporters name the same laureates (B005: Pakes, Berry, Levinsohn; B014: Persson, Tabellini, Besley; B027: Kiyotaki, Moore; B030: Autor, Hanson, Dorn). The disagreements are across ballots and over who is excluded, not between supporters of the same ballot.

Members cite the same common criteria (originality, attribution clarity, maturity and validation, breadth of impact), and each leading position's own proponents state its principal weakness. They weigh the criteria differently.

B005 is named by all eleven members as either a preferred part or an alternative (six as alternative: Boppart, Dreber, Fredriksson, Hassler, Hjalmarsson, Krusell). Alternatives are not counted as support here, and some of these members state limited familiarity (Dreber, Hjalmarsson) or reservations.
Several members explicitly describe two or more of the leading candidates as close or serious (Hassler on B005, Krusell on B005 and B014, Fredriksson on B005, Hjalmarsson and Dreber on B005).
Several members describe B036 as having diffuse attribution that a three-name cap cannot resolve without contested omissions (Andersson, Hassler, Strömberg).
scientific_disputes: Methods versus discovery: B005 supporters hold that a measurement tool that changes what can be credibly known is itself a discovery (Teorell, Enflo, Friberg). Others treat a toolkit as weighable against substantive findings (Fredriksson, Hassler, Krusell), and Boppart ranked it eighth in his opening.

Common test: breadth of validated use across fields (B005 supporters) versus conceptual originality and durable influence on how a field thinks (Krusell, Boppart) versus explanatory power on policy-relevant substantive questions (Fredriksson, Hassler, Hjalmarsson). Members have not yet agreed on one test applied to all four.

Identification standard: B014's constitutional and electoral-rule evidence is largely cross-country and observational. Fredriksson, Hassler, Teorell and Friberg state this concern, and B014 supporters contend the theory, within-country and state-capacity strands are less exposed. This remains open.

B027's amplification mechanism is better established theoretically than by direct identification. Supporters and critics agree on this and differ on how much it should count for a contribution of this age.

B030: the size and persistence of China-shock effects and shift-share identification are still debated. Supporters read this as a dispute over magnitudes, not existence. It is also unresolved whether the technology (task) and trade-shock strands form one prize motivation or two (Hjalmarsson, Dreber, Strömberg).

BLP-type estimates are sensitive to functional form, instruments and implementation. Boppart and Dreber treat this as a material reservation. Andersson, Friberg and Teorell read it as evidence of mature scrutiny.
attribution_disputes: B005 third name and scope: all five supporters now name Levinsohn. Friberg's opening favoured Bresnahan, and Andersson, Strömberg and Teorell acknowledge that Bresnahan (and Reiss, Benkard, Levin) have real claims. Several say a Bresnahan or Reiss credit would need a different, broader empirical-IO citation rather than a substitution.

B027: Strömberg's opening added Gertler as a third laureate for the financial accelerator, and in round 1 he describes himself as less comfortable with that. Boppart, Krusell and Teorell oppose adding Gertler or Gilchrist, citing the Bernanke overlap and Gertler's credit being spread across B027 and B036. Whether omitting the accelerator strand is an attribution gap remains an uncertainty.

B030: Dorn versus Katz as third name. Boppart's opening had Katz and his round 1 says Dorn should be preferred if B030 is pursued. Hjalmarsson and Dreber exclude Katz because of overlap with the Goldin-related strand. Credit for the task framework also extends to Levy, Murnane and Acemoglu, who are not on the ballot, as Dreber and Hjalmarsson note.

B014: whether Besley belongs in the same award as Persson-Tabellini, or whether a two-person Persson-Tabellini award is cleaner (Fredriksson). Alesina, Drazen and Acemoglu-Robinson-type work is cited as nearby, but not as a proposal.

B025 (an alternative for Enflo, Fredriksson and Friberg, not a preferred part): Boppart and Friberg raise Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum as an uncredited parallel contribution. Enflo says this moved her away from B025.
maturity_disputes: B014: the programme is about thirty years old and its maturity is not disputed. Whether it is distinct enough from the 2024 institutions prize is disputed (flagged by Fredriksson, Hassler, Teorell, Friberg, Strömberg, Enflo and Andersson). Supporters distinguish policy choice under given rules from long-run origins of institutions, and Enflo says Besley's state-capacity strand sits closer to the 2024 agenda.

B027: about three decades old with no timing concern. The dispute is distinctness from the 2022 prize (raised by Enflo, who ranked it eighth in her opening, and by Andersson, Krusell, Boppart, Hassler and Teorell). Boppart and Krusell argue the mechanisms differ (bank runs and intermediation versus collateral-constrained borrowers).

B030: roughly two decades old and replicated, but Fredriksson and Strömberg describe it as only moderately mature, and its main reservations concern persistence and shift-share identification. Overlap with the 2023 and 2024 prizes is also raised.

B009: Hassler ranked it last of his eight in the opening on recency and unfinished long-run assessment. Dreber, its opening first choice, accepted much of this and moved to B030, listing B009 as an alternative. No member lists B009 as a preferred part in round 1.
B005: no member raises a timing concern. Andersson, Enflo and Strömberg describe about three decades of use and critique.
Claims about replication records and prior prizes come from members' own statements, and several members say they did not verify them independently. This summary does not verify them either.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Chair (Hassler): prefers B014 (disclosed here). He works in dynamic political economy, which is field proximity to B014, and his profile lists co-authorship with Boppart, Friberg and Krusell and IIES collegiality with Krusell and Boppart. He reports no co-authorship or institutional tie to Persson, Tabellini or Besley. Disclosed, not adjudicated.

Krusell and Boppart: both prefer B027. Boppart states he is a long-running co-author of Krusell and Hassler, and Krusell lists Boppart and Hassler as co-authors. Boppart cautions that agreement among these colleagues is not independent confirmation. Boppart is also a long-running co-author of Klenow (B046), which is not a preferred part.

Friberg: research in industrial organisation and pricing is field proximity to B005, which he discloses. He reports no tie to any shortlisted candidate. He has co-authored with Hassler and Ellingsen (IJIO).

Teorell: field proximity to B014 (democratisation and institutions) and delivered the 2024 institutions presentation speech. His round 1 states his profile names no tie to Persson, Tabellini or Besley, whereas Hassler's round 1 refers to a possible Persson link disclosed in Teorell's opening. These two statements are not reconciled in the files.

Fredriksson, Andersson, Enflo, Strömberg, Dreber, Hjalmarsson: no tie to a credited name on their preferred or alternative ballots is reported. Disclosed institutional or field proximities are Stockholm University and IIES overlap (Fredriksson), Lund (Andersson, Enflo), Chicago Booth adjunct (Strömberg), labour economics (Hjalmarsson) and behavioural economics near B002, which is not a preferred part (Dreber). None are adjudicated.
questions_for_round2: Methods versus discovery: what single test should the Committee apply to B005, B014, B027 and B030 alike (for example, did the work change what can be credibly known, and has it been validated in use or evidence)? Can members state how each of the four candidates fares under that same test, not under the criterion most favourable to their own first choice?

B005 scope: should the citation rest on the Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes demand-estimation core (with or without dynamic industry models, as in Teorell's wording), or on the broader empirical-IO tradition that would bring in Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard or Levin? Would any supporter change the laureate set if the wording were widened?

B014 identification and credit: which parts of the Persson-Tabellini and Besley programme rest on identification strong enough to support a Nobel citation? Would Fredriksson and Hassler accept a two-person Persson-Tabellini core, and how would the citation avoid overclaiming causal findings?

Prior-prize overlap: for B014 (2024 institutions), B027 (2022 banks and financial crises) and B030 (2023 and 2024), should overlap count as a bar or as a weight against marginal contribution? Can members state specifically what each candidate adds that the earlier prize did not cover, and note which parts of that argument they have not verified?

B027 accelerator strand: is a two-person Kiyotaki-Moore award complete without Gertler or Gilchrist, given the stated Bernanke overlap and Gertler's credit being spread across B027 and B036? Is Strömberg's withdrawal of the Gertler proposal confirmed?

B030 credit and coherence: if B030 is pursued, is Dorn preferred to Katz as third name, and do the technology (task) and trade-shock strands support one citation, or would the China-shock work alone be the better-attributed piece?

Movement between positions: Hassler, Fredriksson, Dreber and Hjalmarsson have each said they would not oppose B005 or would move to it under stated conditions. What specific evidence or argument in round 2 would lead members of the B005, B014, B027 and B030 camps to revise their preferred part, and what would not?

Conflicts: should Teorell clarify the discrepancy between his stated absence of a Persson link and Hassler's reference to one? Does any member think the co-authorship cluster (Hassler, Krusell, Boppart, Friberg) or the field proximities listed above should change how those members' arguments are weighed? The simulation protocol records conflicts without adjudicating them.
summary.chair_observation: No ballot has six explicit first-choice supporters in round 1. B005 has five, and B014, B027 and B030 have two each. Within each ballot supporters name identical laureates, so the open questions are mainly cross-ballot (breadth of validated use, conceptual originality, substantive findings, identification strength, overlap with recent prizes), plus who is left out of each credit set. Alternatives are not votes, and I draw no inference about unstated preferences or from nomination frequency. I prefer B014 and disclose that, so this summary relies only on positions stated in the files. Claims about prior prizes, replication and citation counts are members' own and are unverified by me.
